title: One Agent Is Powerful. But What About a TEAM?

panels.speaker: AURORA

panels.text: In 2021, Copilot gave developers a taste of AI-assisted coding — magical, but fundamentally autocomplete. In 2022, ChatGPT proved you could describe what you wanted in English and get working code — but the copy-paste cycle was maddening. In 2023, tool use cracked the glass. In 2024-2025, full coding agents put it all together.

panels.caption: The thread through computing history: from Turing's tape to autonomous agents

panels.prompt: A dramatic split-screen comparison. Left side: a single agent (small glowing figure) drowning at a massive desk, papers everywhere, contradicting notes scattered around, overwhelmed expression, dim and chaotic lighting, red stress glow. Right side: five smaller agents, each calm and focused at their own clean desk, each working on one piece of a puzzle -- one reading docs, one writing code, one running tests, one reviewing, one coordinating. An orchestrator figure at the center connects them with flowing violet lines. Files and documents flow between them in an orderly pattern. Bright, organized, productive violet glow. The contrast is striking: chaos vs. harmony. Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes, red on left, violet (#9F7AEA) on right

panels.text: The solution? The same one humans discovered thousands of years ago. You do not build a cathedral with one brilliant architect. You build it with a team — specialists who each focus on what they know best, coordinated by someone who holds the big picture.

What if you had a researcher agent that digs into documentation, a coder agent that writes the implementation, a tester agent that writes tests, and a reviewer agent that catches bugs — each with a fresh, clean context, each working in parallel, none weighed down by each other’s noise? That is not science fiction. That is what is happening right now.

panels.prompt: A small cute round bright-violet robot with a dome head and big excited white LED eyes, stubby arms holding a tiny blueprint labeled MULTI-AGENT SYSTEM, antenna with a tiny constellation of stars on top, smaller robots forming a coordinated formation behind it. A white speech bubble with black outline above. Inside the bubble the text reads: "The answer was there all along: divide the work." Comic book style, warm editorial illustration with ink lines and watercolor washes
panels.bubble_text: The answer was there all along: divide the work.
panels.speaker: SOLVEBOT

panels.text: The progression from autocomplete to agents is not just a story about AI getting smarter. It is a story about AI getting closer to doing real work in the real world. Each leap closed another gap between “thinking about code” and “doing the work.” But the final gap — between a brilliant solo performer and an effective team — is still being closed.

panels.text: In our next issue, the solo agent becomes a swarm. Multiple agents, working in parallel, communicating through files, each with a fresh context and a focused task. The pattern will look familiar — because it is the Unix philosophy, reborn in a new form. Issue 9: "The Swarm."
